title: Kernel Policy Synthesizer for Burst Latency Smoothing
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Problem: We observe intermittent token-tail spikes during short high-throughput bursts for conversational workloads. Existing approach selects kernels per-request using a seqlen-arch heuristic, but it can oscillate under bursty arrival patterns and occasionally choose kernels that increase tail latency when occupancy/streaming dynamics change. Goal: Build a lightweight online "Kernel Policy Synthesizer" that generates a safety-constrained kernel-switching policy per-GPU-pool. The synthesizer uses short horizon burst forecasts + a simulated annealing style policy search with explicit safety margins to reduce tail latency while keeping median cost neutral. It must be realtime-safe (<=200us decision overhead) and provide deterministic fallbacks to robust kernel variants (e.g., quantized/fallback-attn) when confidence is low. This ticket captures design, a prototype, evaluation, and rollout plan.
acceptance_criteria: Prototype runs in runtime-staging with <=200us decision latency for policy lookup and switch
P95 token latency for bursty benchmark workload reduced by >=15% compared to current seqlen-heuristic baseline
Overall token cost delta within +/-3% on average across benchmark set
Safety fallback engages on anomalous telemetry and prevents latency regressions in at least 3 recorded failure modes
Telemetry surfaces per-policy decisions and confidence scores in Console runtime dashboard
tasks: Design policy representation: compact rule set + confidence score (2d)
Implement burst detector and short-horizon seqlen forecast (sliding window, lightweight EWMA + quantiles)
Implement synthesizer: simulated annealing search over kernel sequences with cost/latency objective and safety constraints
Integrate policy into runtime decision path with microsecond budget and safe rollback hook
Add telemetry hooks: policy_id, decision_time_us, confidence, pre/post-latency samples
Benchmark on mixed workloads (conversation bursts, docs summarization, embeddings) and produce report
Create canary rollout plan and dashboard in Console for monitoring
Write docs + runbook for incidents (how to force-disable synthesizer and revert to static heuristic)
notes: Design choices: prefer a small policy cache keyed by (gpu_type, model_family, burst_profile) rather than per-customer policies to limit memory and cold-starts
Safety margins: require predicted latency improvement > 10ms and confidence >= 0.7 to switch to an aggressive kernel; otherwise stick to conservative kernel or quantized fallback
Decision complexity budget: target <200us so we avoid contributing to request latency; heavy search should run asynchronously to refine policies
We will use existing microbench harness and prefetched KV traces from telemetry to simulate bursts offline before applying live

Avoid per-token switching; policy applies at request-level and persists for request lifetime. Consider prefill/decode split: allow different kernels for prefill vs decode phases if confidence supports it
success_metrics: P95 token latency reduction on CONV-BURST benchmark >=15%
P99 non-regression for stable workloads (<=2% increase)
Policy false-switch rate <2% (switches that lead to immediate rollback)
test_plan: Offline: run synthesizer on historical telemetry traces to validate objective convergence and safety triggers
Perf CI: add microbench scenario for 1s and 5s burst windows with mixed seqlen distribution
Staging canary: enable on 5% of traffic for a small GPU pool, monitor latency & errors for 72h
Gradual rollout: 5% -> 25% -> 60% -> 100% with rollbacks automated on SLO violations
rollout: Stage 0: deploy synthesizer as opt-in behind runtime flag to staging clusters
Stage 1: Canary on a low-traffic GPU pool (5%) with alerting for P95 regressions
Stage 2: Expand to mixed pools with adaptive confidence thresholds
Stage 3: Full rollout with default conservative thresholds; enable aggressive mode via config for specific model families
risks: Incorrect forecast can cause unnecessary kernel oscillation and worsen tail latency
Decision code path adds CPU overhead on hot path if not carefully optimized
Overfitting policies to synthetic traces; may not generalize to customer burst patterns
Telemetry gaps may cause stale policies to be applied — need freshness checks and TTL
mitigations: Maintain conservative default policy; require multiple corroborating signals before aggressive switches
Keep policy evaluation micro-optimized in C++ hot path; run heavier searches in background
Use cross-validation on held-out traces and shadow mode to detect overfitting
Add policy TTL and simple revert-to-default when telemetry heartbeat missing for >60s
